# Gelabber v0.6.0

Integrated through the feature PRs #189, #191, #192 and #193 and the sync of
`main` (#198, with #183, #185 and #186) into `v0.6`, and the version PR #194
into `main`.

**Operators: read "Upgrade and operation" first.** v0.6 no longer starts
without your own passwords in `.env`, the bundled Caddy listens on
`127.0.0.1` by default, and the proxy must be recreated for the new
Caddyfile.

## Web client and phone PWA

- Gelabber can be installed from a phone's browser: manifest with icons,
  a passive service worker that only keeps an offline page (app pages, API,
  media and assets stay on the network), an install panel on the login page
  and under **Einstellungen → App** where the browser offers it, and the
  steps for iPhone/iPad. Requires HTTPS on the phone (see below).
- Message notifications on phones go through the service worker, sound and
  vibrate once per message, are not raised for a conversation another window
  shows, and a tap opens the conversation without a reload. A window that
  catches up after a reconnect does not announce older messages again.
- Phone layout: notch and keyboard insets, 16 px fields and 44 px touch
  targets, a composer that keeps the keyboard open and grows, the screen
  stays on during calls, call controls and toasts keep clear of each other on
  a phone lying on its side, an unread dot on the navigation button.
- Camera, screen share and Go Live are offered only where they can start, and
  say why not. A share or Go Live that cannot be captured says so; closing the
  picker says nothing. A Go Live that never starts releases the channel.
- Stream sound is a choice of its own, next to the share button, and on by
  default where the call stays out of it. It survives a rollback to v0.5.x
  and the way back.
- Paste an image from the clipboard into the composer (Strg+V), or drop a
  file anywhere on the conversation, to attach it; Enter sends it. A file
  dropped elsewhere no longer replaces the app.
- The call card's volume rows line up, use slim theme-coloured sliders, and no
  longer give the channel list a horizontal scrollbar during a stream.
- The message cache stays bounded: channels that are not open keep only
  small tombstones, each channel at most 500 entries, the newest page at
  its page size, and previews of sent images are released. Long sessions no
  longer grow by about 22 MB per 50,000 events.
- **Profil → Sicherheit:** change your password (ends every other session)
  and sign out everywhere.
- Plain-http servers on an address other than localhost can no longer log in
  (deliberate; see "Security").

## Security (#188)

- **No default passwords.** `POSTGRES_PASSWORD`, `MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD` and
  `TURN_PASSWORD` (and `GRAFANA_ADMIN_PASSWORD` with observability) must be
  set in `.env`; `docker compose` stops with a message otherwise.
- **Plain HTTP on the server's own machine only.** The bundled Caddy listens
  on `127.0.0.1` by default (`GELABBER_HTTP_BIND`). Without
  `API_COOKIE_SECURE=true` the API signs in only on `localhost`; other
  machines get `insecure_transport`. Put TLS in front and set
  `API_COOKIE_SECURE=true`; `API_ALLOW_PLAIN_HTTP=true` is for a trusted test
  network only.
- Behind TLS the API sends HSTS and refuses to start while a former
  repository default password is still set.
- Sign-in protection per account as well as per address: 10 failures lock the
  account for 15 minutes. The client address is the rightmost
  `X-Forwarded-For` entry.
- Backups can be encrypted with age (`GELABBER_BACKUP_AGE_RECIPIENT`).
- `rustls` 0.23.45 (RUSTSEC-2026-0285).

## Linux desktop app

- Files dropped from the file manager attach to the message, as in the
  browser.

- Video inside the app window: cameras and streams of others in their tiles
  and in the large view, the own camera and the own stream as previews. A
  stream in its own viewer window is not drawn in the page as well.
- The viewer window draws on the right GPU (no black window next to an iGPU).
- Stream sound without the call's echo: "every application" leaves out
  Gelabber's own playout and virtual devices' playback, keeps network
  receivers, and is on by default with a switch next to the share button.
- A crashed web process no longer leaves capture running behind a dead view;
  closing the window no longer crashes WebKit on NVIDIA.
- Native core with C ABI 8 (`media_view_*` commands, local video sinks). Web
  clients and apps keep working across versions: the server's web client asks
  the app for its features and still serves 0.5.x apps (ABI 7), and a v0.6 app
  works with an older server's web client.

## Windows desktop app (new)

- Installer `gelabber-desktop-windows-x64-setup.exe` (NSIS, per user, no
  admin rights, WebView2 bootstrapper) with a `.sha256` file. The native core
  ships as `gelabber_media.dll`. Unsigned: SmartScreen asks once
  ("Weitere Informationen" → "Trotzdem ausführen").
- Chat, voice through the native core, camera and watching cameras and streams
  inside the app work. Screen share and Go Live go through the system's
  capture picker (Windows.Graphics.Capture, Windows 10 1903 or later), with
  application sound through WASAPI process loopback (every application or a
  chosen one, never the call itself; Windows 10 2004 or later, otherwise the
  share goes on without sound).
- Tested by the maintainers with `v0.6.0-alpha.1` on real Windows hardware
  (reported as passed on 2026-10-12; no per-item results recorded). That
  alpha had no screen share, Go Live or application sound on Windows.

## Upgrade and operation

- **Restart the bundled proxy for the new Caddyfile.** The Caddyfile now hands
  on `Host` with its port (`{hostport}`) and compresses responses; a
  `caddy reload` keeps the old file. After switching the checkout to the tag:
  `docker compose --env-file .env --env-file next.env up -d --no-deps --force-recreate proxy`.
  Only where the bundled Caddy runs: **not with `compose.homelab.yaml`**, where
  that command would start the bundled Caddy on `0.0.0.0:80`. Homelab
  operators carry the `Caddyfile.homelab` change into their own Caddy
  (`deploy/README.md`).
- **Outer proxies must hand on the browser's `Host`, port included.** `/ws`
  compares `Origin` with `Host`; a proxy that writes the upstream's or another
  internal port into `Host` now gets 403 on every WebSocket (chat stops
  updating, voice does not connect). The API logs the refused Origin and Host.
- **Set the passwords in `.env` before `docker compose up`**, and decide how
  other machines reach the server: the default now listens on `127.0.0.1`
  only and signs in on `localhost` only. For the LAN or the internet put TLS
  in front and set `API_COOKIE_SECURE=true` (`deploy/README.md`, "Security").
  An existing Postgres volume keeps its password until
  `ALTER USER gelabber PASSWORD '…'`. Behind TLS the API refuses to start
  with `gelabber`, `gelabbergelabber`, `gelabberturn` or `change-me…`.
- **HTTPS for phones.** Service worker, install, microphone and notifications
  need a secure context, so phones need a TLS endpoint in front
  (`docs/v0.6-pwa.md`).
- **A Content-Security-Policy must let the app's IPC through:** add `ipc:`
  and `http://ipc.localhost` to `connect-src`, or in-app video stays at
  320×180, 15 fps.
- Third-party notices ship in every desktop package
  (`THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt`).
- No migrations. The image set moves to `v0.6.0` together.
  Rolling back to v0.5.2 touches no data, but the checkout (and with it the
  Caddyfile) goes back to the old tag too and the proxy is restarted the same
  way: an API before 0.6 refuses `Host` with the default port.

## Open

- Not tested: real Android and iOS devices, a real webcam, element
  fullscreen in the app, the real portal picker, the Windows capture picker
  (CI captures the primary monitor without it; `v0.6.0-alpha.1` had no
  screen share), application sound of a real program on Windows (CI checks
  the loopback without one) and real speakers, GPUs other than one NVIDIA
  RTX 5080 on Hyprland, sessions longer than 21 minutes, a real file drop
  from the file manager in the Linux app.
- Plain-http servers on a non-localhost address cannot log in (deliberate:
  `insecure_transport` from the API, and the Web Locks guard in
  `withSessionCookieLock`).
- No email verification or password reset yet (#195), no bucket-scoped MinIO
  user for the API (#196), and the native core's transceivers are not
  released during a call (#197).
- A killed Linux app (SIGTERM, end of session) after video still lets
  WebKit's web process crash in the NVIDIA driver; a closed window does not.
- Video in the Linux app costs about 34 % + 25 % of a core (app + web
  process) for one 720p20 tile; a maximised window on a 4K monitor was not
  measured.
- The self view shows the encoder-adapted picture, so its size can change
  during a call. Pictures below about 480×270 are sent as the low layer only.
- Go Live does nothing, without a hint, while someone else is live. Image
  attachments open through `target=_blank`. A microphone prompt still open
  during a media reconnect loses the microphone silently.
- The browser smoke tests (PWA, in-app video, phone layout) do not run in CI.
- H264/FFmpeg/OpenH264 licensing of the Linux package (#165) is undecided;
  the Windows DLL carries no H264 code. The repository has no LICENSE file.
